LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.expectedCodewordL: For a finite source with distribution p and binary words assigned on its positive support, the expected codeword length in bits is L(c) = ∑ₐ p(a) length(c(a)), summed over the supported symbols.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.natsToBits_entrop: Every binary prefix code on the positive support of a finite source p satisfies L(c) ≥ H(p)/ln 2, where the entropy H is in nats and L is in bits.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_isBinaryPr: There is a binary prefix code on the positive support of p with each length equal to ⌈−log₂ p(a)⌉ and expected length strictly less than H(p)/ln 2 + 1 bits.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.optimalPrefixLeng: For a finite source p, L*(p) is the infimum of expected binary codeword lengths over prefix codes on precisely the symbols of positive probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isLeast_optimalPr: For a finite source p there exists a binary prefix code with mean length L*(p), and every prefix code on the supported symbols has mean length at least L*(p).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.optimalPrefixLeng: For a finite source p the optimal expected binary prefix length satisfies H(p)/ln 2 ≤ L*(p) < H(p)/ln 2 + 1 bits.
